column1: # boru Language Specification: error raising and loud failures
# `raise` constructs the same Ideal/Error the runtime produces and
# raises it: uncaught it aborts with [boru/<code>]; `do [body] error
# [handler]` catches it as an Error value carrying code, message, and
# any extra spec-map payload keys (design/legacy/ERRORS.8.ignore §2, T9.6).
# Also pinned here: the §3 blame-shift fix (a paren expression that
# produces NO value is reported at the causing site) and the §5

column3: a bare message raises code user_error
a bare word names the code
the spec-map form
code and message are both required in the map form
a non-string/map operand has no raise sig

column1: # §2  catching — one error [handler] form for native AND user errors

column3: a raised error is caught like a native one
an error-ignoring handler compiles as a closure; the unconsumed error strips from the residual bottom
a consuming handler over a value-divergent body
an empty handler passes the caught error through as the result

column1: def e (do [raise bad_input "nope"]) e dot code
column3: the code is dispatchable on the caught value
…and the message reads via dot access

column1: def e (do [raise {code: bad_input/q, message: "m", got: 42}]) e dot got
column3: extra spec-map keys ride along for the handler

column1: def e (do [raise {code: bad_input/q, message: "m", got: 42}]) convert Map e
column3: convert Map projects code, message, and payload

column1: def e (do [1 div 0]) convert Map e
column3: arith errors carry the arith_error code (phase-5 taxonomy normalisation)
an unknown key reads as none, mirroring map reads

column1: # §3  void argument expressions are blamed at the causing site

column3: def of a void expression errors at the def, naming the binding
a void group starving any word is named at the call
…but a void group with stack operands available stays valid
…and collection legitimately resumes past a void group

column1: # §4  typed error handling — dispatch on the error with `case`
#     (the error handler runs with the Error on the stack; `get code`
#     consumes it and the stack-value form of case dispatches on the
#     code; or keep the Error as the case value and match it with
#     predicates, the blocks reading its fields).
do [raise bad_input "nope"] error [dot code case [bad_input/q "rejected" io_error/q "retry" "unexpected"]]
column3: dispatch on the code atom

column1: do [raise io_error "disk"] error [dot code case [bad_input/q "rejected" io_error/q "retry" "unexpected"]]
column3: …each code takes its own clause

column1: do [raise weird "?"] error [dot code case [bad_input/q "rejected" io_error/q "retry" "unexpected"]]
column3: …unknown codes take the default

column1: do [raise {code: too_big/q, message: "out of range", limit: 99}] error [case [[dot code eq bad_input/q] [dot message] [dot code eq too_big/q] [dot limit] "unexpected"]]
column3: predicate matches inspect the Error itself; the block reads its payload
a successful body skips the handler entirely (error passes the value through)
